parsed.explanation: The dossier documents a trans-specific offence on the books (Section 379, criminalising male presentation as female, up to three months' imprisonment) with no documented enforcement of it, and a dead-letter same-sex conduct statute. But surrounding signals are damning: security forces were reported across 2018–2022 to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ persons; a minister publicly ordered detention of LGBTQ persons; the head of state voices hostility; no support organisations exist, and the one community group was raided into closure; most openly LGBTQI+ citizens have fled. No hate-crime or anti-discrimination recourse operates. This is state-tolerated targeting with no remedy — the 0.25 profile (Lemora/B): no enforced presentation offence, but documented police violence, hostile rhetoric, and zero recourse. The dress provision is a latent trans-facing lever in a state that abuses LGBTQI+ people with impunity. A trans visitor outed faces harassment, extortion, possible detention and torture, with no protection. Severity (severe, tier 4) is tempered by the absence of documented executions or routine prosecutions of the dress offence. Thin-data extrapolation from structural facts — criminalisation on the books, hostile state, no community infrastructure, no relief — resolves to high risk, not below 0.20.
